made: node docs/proyecto/pixel/parada-sheet-make.js, from parada-set.html (window.PARADA.E, calle-base.js) and the design of La parada (p5-spec). A new scene: no old scene, no remap.

rules.project: pp-engine.js project(x, y, z) with S 26 and this origin: sx = OX + (x - y) / R2 * S, sy = OY + ((x + y) / R2 * .5 - z * COS) * S, depth d = (x + y) / R2 * COS + z * .5 (R2 = sqrt 2, COS = sqrt 3 / 2); OX = W / 2 + originX, OY = H / 2 + originY. A box is the screen bounding box of its 8 projected corners [floor(min x), floor(min y), ceil(max x) - floor(min x), ceil(max y) - floor(min y)]. screen is the projection rounded to whole pixels. The houses' wall is y = 0 (it faces +y); the street runs from y 1.6 to 5.6, the stop's lane is y 4.6, the near pavement from y 5.8 to 9.2
rules.spot: a spot is a world point of the feet (z 0: the pavement; z 0.46: the seat's top) and, drawn there, a character stands with its feet (the lowest row the sprite draws, outline included) resting on the screen row sy, i.e. the sprite's bottom edge on sy, and its middle column on the column sx (rules.anchor). scale is the frog's: 1 everywhere. kind: person (a character stands there), seat (sits on the seat's top), door (a person stepping on or off at the guagua's door, y 5.45, in front of its lit side 5.25), button (a point on the guagua's side, no sprite), head (a head at the guagua's glass: a sprite detail, the point is the middle of the face), vehicle (the guagua's middle), exit (where something leaves the picture). who: the width class of the sprite box (the frog 32, a grown-up 24, a child 24, a dog 28); sprite: the box the make takes the sprite to fill, [x0, y0, x1, y1] from the spot's column and row (the spec's width and the real drawn pixels)
rules.anchor: the column of the sprite that is on sx; its feet (its lowest drawn row, outline included) rest on row sy - 1, so its bottom edge is on sy. mkPersona (48 wide): column 24 (KIT.PX), 53 rows drawn standing (a 56-row canvas whose lowest row is empty: the lowest drawn row is 54), sitting (sent = 1) the same column, its bottom edge on the seat's top; abuela standing mkAbuela (48 x 51): column 30, drawn rows 0 to 49; abuela sitting KIT.mkAbuelaS (52 x 50): column 17, its bottom edge on the seat's top; the frog mkCoqui(1) (32 x 27): column 16, drawn rows 1 to 24 (so row 25 of the canvas is on sy); Canelo KIT.mkPerro (30 x 22): column 13, its bottom edge on sy; a small thing: its bottom middle on the point; a head at the glass: the middle of the face on the point (abuela mkAbuela row 12 of the canvas, column 30; persona row 11, column 24), shown only through a pane of the guagua's window
rules.view: a view has a zoom (here 1: the 196 x 216 window over the 240 x 216 picture) and x0, the window's left edge. Never a fraction
rules.depth: a spot's depth is the engine's d of its world point; front.plane turns it into the depth of each row of a character
rules.guagua: a guagua at the stop stands with its middle at (P, 4.6), heading i (towards -x): its front end is its -x end; the front door is 0.35 to 1.15 and the back door 3.2 to 4 from the front end, the buttons 1.32 and 3.04 from the front end at z 0.8. puerta_sube is the door at x P - 1.45, puerta_baja at x P + 1.4, a person stepping on or off stands at y 5.45; the frog at a button at (the button's x, 5.9), between the buttons at (P, 5.9). The waiting row is y 7 (fila1 to fila5)

front.how: no list. A character is hidden by every set pixel that is nearer the camera than the character's feet (depth test against the baked depth, with the feet's depth plus 0.3), so the seat hides nothing that stands in front of it and a person at the kerb is in front of the guagua (its lit side is y 5.25).
front.plane: for the character's pixel on picture row r (r = 0 at the top): depth(r) = d + (sy - (r + .5)) * tan(30 deg) / S, where d is the spot's depth and sy its screen row; the pixel is hidden where bakedZ[r * 240 + x] > depth(r) + bias (bakedZ: window.DEPTH.z of the set page). The same rule as El mostrador's sheet: the upright plane through the feet
front.sprites: between two sprites the nearer pixel wins: the same depth(r), no bias

shadows.at: castShadow(x, y, z, radius) at the world x, y, z of the spot (z 0 on the pavement, z 0.46 on the seat), for a character that stands, sits or lies
shadows.note: a head at the guagua's glass casts none
